teams.synopsis: Still on top with the most points in the league — Herbert's health is the only real cloud.
teams.blurb: At the top of the list for the second straight week, this team is dominating the league through two weeks, and it doesn't look like they're slowing down. With the most PF out of all teams so far (278.92), ‘I KNOW WHAT ITS LIKE TO LOSE’ is making it look like it's finally their year to win the PFFL Championship. Be sure to monitor the Justin Herbert injury, but even if it does hinder his fantasy ability, this team will have no problem staying competitive. Jahan Dotson is another player to look out for on Sunday because he's the WR15 on the year, and many are wondering if he is a sustainable flex option for Baylen, with three touchdowns on the season already.

teams.synopsis: The other 2-0-caliber team — unlucky, loaded at the top, and armed with the league's best depth.
teams.blurb: Might be a shock that the other 2-0 team isn't ranked here, but don't underestimate Bileydi's team. This team is tied for the highest RPR (5 players), meaning he has the most 'top tier' fantasy players at their positions compared to the rest of the league. Bileydi is also ranked this high because he has the 4th-most points against through two weeks while having the 2nd-highest PFAA in the league — meaning that despite getting scored on a lot, he's scored the 2nd-most points, putting himself in a position to win every week. With that logic, you might infer that his Week 1 loss was very unlucky, and that if he and McQuaid's team switched schedules, he could be 2-0. Another thing to note: this team has the highest Depth Rating in the league, so he could very easily make deals in the upcoming weeks that make his lineup even scarier.

teams.synopsis: Undefeated without the superstar names — Wentz, Waddle, and Freiermuth are doing the heavy lifting.
teams.blurb: The only other 2-0 team in the league finds its way into the number-three spot on my list, which is a very fair ranking. Alright, Breece's Pieces may not have the superstar names you'd expect from an undefeated team, but he's got top players like Wentz, Waddle, and Freiermuth that have helped elevate him to this ranking. I think the only way for McQuaid to reach the number-2 or even number-1 spot next week is for either of the teams listed above to have a bad week, or if Henry steps up and plays like the player he was drafted to be. That being said, McQuaid's players have tough matchups this week, and it may be hard for the team to produce numbers similar to those posted in Weeks 1 and 2.

teams.synopsis: The week's biggest riser — nine spots up on the strength of Hill, St. Brown, and a breakout Wilson.
teams.blurb: The biggest jump made by any team this week — The Minutemen find themselves up nine spots after a stellar performance, with promising players beginning to take shape. The WR corps of Hill and St. Brown strikes fear into any fantasy manager, but the rising star of Wilson should be even scarier. This team has an even boom-to-bust ratio (6:6), meaning it's one of the most consistent teams — we could predict what we're getting out of this team going forward much more easily than others. Brandon's team also has some of the best depth in the league, so he could make moves in future weeks if he feels they're necessary, but until then, look for this team to rise up the ranks even more if Najee can step up.

teams.synopsis: A step back on paper only — the league's best TE and a Pittman return keep this team dangerous.
teams.blurb: They took a step back this week, but still a very solid team on paper. After making a trade with Carmine last to lock up the league's best TE, this team doesn't have many flaws. Having the most points against through two weeks can be looked at as unlucky, but this team failed to reach 100 points last week, so they would've lost anyway. With <mark class="hl-player">Michael Pittman</mark> returning this week and favorable matchups for most players on the team, look for this team to try and regain its spot higher up the list. Also, if <mark class="hl-player">James Robinson</mark> can keep up his top-10 RB year, or at least be a high-end RB2, this team might be one of the top teams to beat.

teams.synopsis: A panned trade is looking like genius — RB1, CMC, and a top-2 Depth Rating now in tow.
teams.blurb: Some called the trade he made last week 'terrible' and an 'L', but after he used his backup QB to trade for the TE10, this team is looking very promising. Having the RB1 on the team, along with <mark class="hl-player">CMC</mark>, is ridiculous by itself, so be on the lookout for this team. My only critique is maybe the lack of talent at WR, but they've been producing numbers, and the only thing stopping them is injuries. This team has the second-best Depth Rating in the league after making the trade last week, so if injuries did occur, they'd be able to handle them. Also, keep an eye on <mark class="hl-player">Russell Wilson</mark> to see if he picks up his production levels in the coming weeks.

teams.synopsis: Called it in Week 1 — Lamar's all-timer and an electric Mike Williams fuel a seven-spot jump.
teams.blurb: The 4th-highest scorer last week earns our 7th spot on the list, making the jump up seven spots. As I predicted in the Week 1 rankings, this team was able to actually put up points this week and show the rest of the league what it's made of. <mark class="hl-player">Mike Williams</mark> had an electric Thursday night, but <mark class="hl-player">Lamar</mark> stole the show with his all-time performance. I'm a believer that this team has what it takes to climb up the ranks even more as the weeks go on, but if injuries occur, I don't know if this team has the depth to handle it. On the bright side, <mark class="hl-player">Smith</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Olave</mark> were able to produce this weekend after being duds last week.

teams.synopsis: An off week exposes the depth chart — a kicker as your #2 scorer isn't a winning formula.
teams.blurb: A fall from grace this past week — Krispy Kareems had an off week, but if he can find a TE to fill in for Schultz and a better WR to replace Woods, this team will be back towards the top. He also needs Fournette to step it up and score some touchdowns — having your second-highest scorer be a kicker isn't great when trying to win a fantasy game. Ben's team has some things to figure out, but look for a bounce back in Week 3.

teams.synopsis: Second in points despite the low ranking — Hurts, Jones, and Kirk make this sustainable.
teams.blurb: The second-highest PF scorer this week may be a little too low for your liking, but I think this is a reasonable placement for a team that had a defense drop 25 points and a kicker put up 17. This team has 3 top-tier players at their positions, including Hurts, Jones, and Kirk, so a high PF week in and week out is very possible for this team. I also feel like this team has the ability to make some moves and upgrade at TE, thanks to the above-average Depth Rating.

teams.synopsis: Eleven busts and counting — unlucky, or just not the team the draft promised?
teams.blurb: This team has the ability to be very good, but then again Penny didn't look very good in Kenneth Walker's debut, and Knox has been subpar even with Josh Allen playing amazing. I think this team has been unlucky with the amount of busts so far (11), including Darnell Mooney, who has been nonexistent this year, but this team also may just not be what we thought it would be coming out of the draft. Maney has above-average depth, so look for him to be engaged with the trade market, especially for a new TE.

teams.synopsis: Four quarterbacks, zero depth — Taylor and Andrews are doing all the heavy lifting now.
teams.blurb: Looks like the 4-QB draft strategy is working out, thanks to <mark class="hl-player">Dak</mark>'s injury last week and <mark class="hl-player">Lance</mark>'s ankle injury in Week 2. This team's bench and depth is awful, and I'm not going to lie — this team looks set up for failure. The only thing stopping me from ranking this team lower is the win from last week, and the fact that <mark class="hl-player">Taylor</mark> and <mark class="hl-player">Andrews</mark> might be enough to win this team a couple of weeks if they both go off. I don't have much to say about Gorman's team, but what I will say is that he'll have to get very lucky, and his players will have to shock the league if he wants to climb back up this list.

teams.synopsis: A trade for CEH softens the blow of the league's second-highest points against.
teams.blurb: As I was making this list, Quigley made a trade to acquire the RB5 on the year, <mark class="hl-player">CEH</mark>. I think this trade was beneficial for him in the short run, but we should monitor <mark class="hl-player">Mitchell</mark> and see how he plays after injury. This team has the second-highest PA in the entire league, meaning he's been scored on a lot — and maybe if he'd been scored on the average amount, he'd have some wins to his name. I think wins will come for this team, but don't be shocked if it's at this spot again next week.

teams.synopsis: Uncharacteristically quiet — the lowest PFAA in the league and no signature trade yet.
teams.blurb: What's going on with him this year? Kelly has been very silent in the PFFL this year, and I think he may be having a down year — even though he's 1-1 — because he hasn't made the trades and big deals we're accustomed to seeing from him. This team has the lowest PFAA among all teams so far, so I wouldn't be surprised if he loses this upcoming week and falls below .500. I don't have many positive things to say about this team, but I guess the depth gives Kelly the opportunity to make trades soon and turn around this awkward roster.

teams.synopsis: Carried by Waller, Cooks, and Kupp alone — the easiest schedule ahead is the only silver lining.
teams.blurb: Of course, man, this manager loves to be down here, and I think this year it's because he drafted an awful team with a bunch of rookies and a reach on Montgomery. Geg's team is carried by Waller, Cooks, and Kupp — which is simply not enough to win matchups. This team also has little to no support on the bench, with a DR of 26.7, which makes it hard to trade, even if he wanted to. That being said, this team has very easy matchups this week and the highest projected points for the upcoming week. Good luck, Geg — you're going to need it.
